purpose: Shared Nostr engine, independent ESP32, Pi, P4 and custom-board signer releases, plus a generic Board/SDK.

status_semantics.planned: Dependencies or resources remain; preparatory research may proceed but acceptance cannot close.
status_semantics.ready: Dependencies integrated and declared resources available; reconcile source and claim scope before assigning.
status_semantics.running: Assigned bounded work on recorded inputs.
status_semantics.blocked: Assigned work stopped on a recorded missing resource or condition and next action.
status_semantics.verified: Acceptance evidence and independent review pass on exact recorded inputs/candidate.
status_semantics.integrated: Verified result integrated with affected integration gates passing.

definition_of_done: Acceptance met on exact candidate commit/artifacts.
Independent review closed for final candidate.
Evidence includes commands/procedures, environment, result and hashes.
Affected integration gates pass after integration.
Documentation and task state agree with source and measurements.
authorization: Maintainer delegated autonomous execution of the complete plan on 2026-10-18, including research, implementation, local engineering, GitHub issues, branches, pull requests, merges, commits and pushes. Reuse this authorization. Specific purchases, fabrication orders, production-secret ceremonies and irreversible provisioning still require a concrete reviewed scope; missing physical evidence cannot be waived.

deferred_tracks.track: Additional board models inside supported families

tasks.title: Make the measured baseline reproducible
acceptance: Fresh isolated checkout installs pinned Python, Node/package manager and Rust toolchains with one documented bootstrap.
Resolve sibling/nested layout explicitly; classify stale API generation and integration launcher noise without weakening behavioral checks.
Run relevant software suites and full integration; record skipped live/physical gates and exact input commits.

tasks.title: Define the retained portfolio and per-profile threat models
acceptance: Adopt or revise the four signer profiles and independent developer platform; smartcards leave active scope without losing history.
For each profile define user flows, custody, active channels, boot integrity, trusted UI, physical attacker assumptions and recovery; do not impose a one-dimensional security ranking.
Connected daily-use profiles include NIP-44; initial QR profiles define manual scope, resource/time limits and explicit unsupported capabilities.
Every required guarantee maps to an acceptance gate and real evidence; unavailable hardware properties are not replaced with booleans or silently waived.

tasks.title: Define compatibility and adoption test plans by profile
acceptance: Choose initial client/version candidates and record source-backed protocol support and known gaps; this is test planning rather than completion of every profile integration.
Define separate connected, QR and Board-developer evidence requirements and success measures; actual client timing/interactions/pilots belong to the corresponding implementation/release tasks.
Prepare opt-in research scripts; participant recruitment and identification of an independent Board developer are performed by the profile that needs them, not a universal prerequisite.
No release waits for observations or a participant from an unrelated profile.

Use client-qualification.md as initial source-backed candidates, reconcile source/lockfiles before execution and test desktop browser versions. Source support is not actual interoperability; pilot numerical goals are hypotheses, not market validation.

tasks.title: Close Bridge identity and bounded-input security gaps
scope: specs independent response metadata oracle and vectors
core snapshot provenance and pinned lab integration consumers
acceptance: Using public fixture keys, reproduce the baseline NIP-46 session-manager acceptance of a changed user signing key and of a foreign signed transport author delivered by an adapter; distinguish this conditional handler gap from exploitability of the default adapter. Pin companion source 13414320537d0208fc3ef8e43bd0723c98c1d5e0 and retain negative regression tests.
Pin authenticated expected signer transport author in the manager itself.
Resolve and bind user identity separately from transport identity; reject unauthorized identity changes and mixed-session/replay responses.
Preserve legal transport/user key separation and verify existing clients and cancellation/error flows.

Reproduce SerialLineStreamPort retaining 20,000 queued bytes from 10,000 short lines with maxBufferedBytes=4; enforce total bytes and request count, backpressure, terminal-error behavior and cleanup, not only per-line limits.

tasks.title: Constrain secret ownership and cryptographic implementation
acceptance: Remove secret-bearing Debug and unnecessary Clone/public secret access; test exposed formatting behavior using public fixture material.
Define lifetimes, copies, zeroization boundaries and internal-memory allocation; do not claim compiler-proof physical erasure from ownership alone.

Select maintained crypto/zeroization candidates using independent vectors, pinned features and no_std compile plus final-link probes for the first target; qualify every actual device in its own implementation/release task, not as a universal prerequisite.

Test raw BIP-340 event-digest signing and NIP-44 unhashed shared-x derivation explicitly; high-level prehash and generic ECDH helpers are not interchangeable. Preserve C/Rust ABI link failures and exact corrected flags when evaluating a C backend.

Specify the entropy-provider boundary and failure contract, including FFI/weak-symbol/runtime fallback risks; define how source-to-final-binary provenance and actual provider invocation will be checked in each device gate.

tasks.title: Make authorization bind exactly one canonical operation
acceptance: Derive identity and canonical event bytes inside the trusted device boundary.
Bind preview, selected identity, full operation and one-use approval; reject mutation, replay, cancellation races and unreviewed metadata.
Bound resource use and handle long/hostile Unicode content without misleading truncation.
An independently computed event ID and signature verifier agree for positive and adversarial vectors.

This task establishes portable authorization/parser semantics with host-executable negative tests. Physical UI/input and peripheral isolation remain each profile's actual-device acceptance; do not wait for all boards to implement the state machine.

Preserve NIP-06 compatibility without treating currently unrecommended derivation as the default; prove expected-public-key recovery.
Independent cryptographic review rejects unsupported non-exportability or dual-SE independence claims.

Specify developer, owner-secured and product-qualified transitions, MCU/SE erasure/re-enrollment and irreversible-state limits. The specification is not evidence that these transitions already work on hardware.

Separate MCU owner firmware roots from vendor-controlled SE applet/update authority; document offline operation, maintenance service, licensing/API access and update/rollback consequences. Specify physical erasure/re-enrollment tests here: MCU feasibility in H02, SE reset/re-enrollment feasibility in H02S, and complete lifecycle in V02/V03.

tasks.title: Complete connected-profile NIP-44 user-message operations

Define device-enforced permissions and leakage boundaries; do not expose stable conversation keys by convenience.

Bare pubkey/payload decrypt methods do not carry signed outer-event context. Distinguish primitive permissions from verified-message operations; never claim an unseen outer signature was device-verified.

For NIP-17/59 bind reviewed recipient/plaintext to ciphertext and the subsequent seal signature; reject opaque or unmatched seal signing rather than blind-signing to satisfy a client. Trace actual client call ordering and cancellation.

Follow current NIP-44 extended-length framing with checked padding arithmetic and pre-allocation product caps; add vectors at 65535/65536 and oversize rejection even if the cap is smaller. Never export conversation keys to remove prompts.

release_gate_template: Exact profile, supported hardware, firmware/SDK/bootloader configuration and declared capabilities are pinned.
Profile-specific custody, transport, boot, physical-attacker and recovery guarantees have measured evidence; unavailable properties are never fabricated as configured or verified.
Independent review closes all applicable blocking findings on the candidate; early engineering uses disposable public identities and formal pilot/real identity admission requires these gates.
Pilot/recovery and independent reproduction meet profile-specific acceptance; security is not waived by satisfaction scores.
Actual release artifacts reproduce, are signed as applicable and have accurate installation/recovery/security documentation.
Publication/order/provisioning actions occur only within applicable authorization; each profile can ship without an unrelated profile passing.
sequencing_note: The connected Bridge integration C01 is first proven on the accessible device V01 and reused by the custom Signer path. This is an implementation sequence, not a claim that the custom-board custody design or generic SDK intrinsically depends on a commercial no-SE board. Pi, P4 and accessible releases do not wait for custom fabrication; Board SDK does not wait for the Nostr app.
